To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the assessment of learning outcomes is an underdeveloped area of practice in public relations education, 2) educators and practitioners agree on the importance of assessment but have different opinions on what assessment protocols are most appropriate, 3) educators place too much emphasis on the use of grades alone as a means of assessing student achievement, 4) educators and practitioners value portfolios, capstone experiences, internships, and surveys of alumni as means of measuring student achievement, 5) educators and

assessment of learning outcomes is a critical component of the public relations educational experience, that it is not being used to any significant extent, that there is a need for greater involvement by practitioners in the assessment process, that there is general agreement about the value of capstones and portfolio assessments as a means of measuring learning outcomes, and that the Assessment Task Team has developed a multidimensional assessment plan that can be adapted by public relations academic programs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how public relations programs are assessing student learning and how they might do it better.
the development of a comprehensive, multidimensional, outcomes-based approach to assessment.

developing an appropriate assessment model that is based on the principles of good practice, that is consistent with current public relations educational practice, that is acceptable to educators and practitioners and that can be used to assess the effectiveness of undergraduate and graduate programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the assessment of public relations programs should be a multidimensional, ongoing process which is designed to measure knowledge, behavior, affect and change.
assessment is a process that can be used to improve programs of study.
the assessment practices and opinions of educators and professionals in the public relations profession are not well aligned, but that there are many common points on which they do agree.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
assessment should be viewed as a process that begins with a clearly articulated set of learning objectives and continues throughout students' academic career.
the assessment process is a continuous, cyclical one.

the assessment of learning outcomes in public relations programs should be based on the following: (1) a clear statement of program outcomes; (2) a variety of assessment tools; (3) the use of multiple measures to assess outcomes; (4) a variety of stakeholders; (5) a focus on the process as well as the product; and (6) the use of assessment results for continuous improvement of programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
assessment is an ongoing process that can be accomplished with a minimum of resources and a maximum of information.
assessment should be a continuous, ongoing, systematic process.
assessment should be a continuous, ongoing process rather than an end-of-program event.
